Short title, extent and commencement

THE PROFESSIONS TAX LIMITATION ACT, 1941
THE PROFESSIONS
TAX LIMITATION ACT, 1941
ACT No. XX of 1941
(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India,
1941, Pt. V, p. 123, and for Report of Select Committee, see ibid., p. 167.
The Act has been applied to Baluchistan, see Notification No.
52‑F, dated the 5th April, 1942, Gazette of India, 1942, Pt. I, p. 682.
It has been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan by
the Leased Areas (Laws) Order, 1950 (G. G. O. 3 of 1950).)
[26th November,
1941]
An Act to limit to
a maximum of fifty rupees per annum the amount
payable in respect of any person by way of tax on
professions, trades, callings or employments.
WHEREAS by section 142A of the
Government of India Act, 26 1935, it is provided that no Provincial law
relating to taxes for (3c the benefit of a Province, or of a municipality,
district board, local board, or other local authority therein, in respect of
pro fessions, trades, callings or employments shall be invalid on the ground
that it relates to a tax on income and that the total amount of such tax
payable in respect of any one person shall not, after the 31st day of March,
1939, exceed fifty rupees per annum; 26 Geo 5,.c.2.
AND WHEREAS it is further
provided in the said section that any such tax which was in force during the
financial year ending with the 31st day of March, 1939, may continue to be
lawfully levied at a rate higher than fifty rupees per annum unless pro vision
to the contrary is made by the Federal Legislature;
AND WHEREAS it is expedient that
provision shall be made whereby the total amount payable in respect of any such
persons by way of such tax shall not exceed fifty rupees per annum;
It is hereby enacted as follows:‑
1. Short title extent and
commencement----‑(1) This Act may be called the Professions Tax Limi tation
Act; 1941.
[(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.]( Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform)
Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th
October, 1955), for the original sub‑section (2), as amended by A. O., 1949.)
(3) It shall come into force on
the 1st day of April, 1942.

Limitation of tax

WHEREAS by section 142A of the

district board, local board, or other local authority therein, in respect of
pro fessions, trades, callings or employments shall be invalid on the ground

AND WHEREAS it is further
provided in the said section that any such tax which was in force during the
financial year ending with the 31st day of March, 1939, may continue to be

AND WHEREAS it is expedient that
provision shall be made whereby the total amount payable in respect of any such
persons by way of such tax shall not exceed fifty rupees per annum;
2. Limitation of tax------Notwithstanding
the provisions of any law for the time being in force, any taxes payable in
respect of any one person to a Province, or to any one municipality, district
board, local board or other local authority in any Province, by way of tax on
professions, trades, callings or employments, shall from and after the
commencement of this Act cease to be levied to the extent to which such taxes
exceed fifty rupees per annum.
